failure_patterns.pattern: cache_contract_violation: A result was not saved, a stale or broad cached base was used, or existing work was repeated instead of applying a delta.

rejected_edits.content: For ratings, treat a single numeric rating without minimum or “at least” language as exact `[x, x]`; “exactly x” is `[x, x]`, and an explicit “at least x” request is `[x, 5]`. For a single approximate budget amount (for example, “around 500 per night”), pass the stated amount to the domain’s numeric `budget` field; do not invent a range or ask for more precision.
rejected_edits.target: For ratings, treat a single numeric rating without minimum or “at least” language as exact `[x, x]`; “exactly x” is `[x, x]`, and an explicit “at least x” request is `[x, 5]`.

rejected_edits.content: If the cache summary lists multiple keys for a pending deliverable, choose the latest, most-refined compatible result for the same domain, location, and itinerary leg that retains all earlier constraints still in force. Retrieve it this turn using its exact listed key and assign the returned result to a variable. For an ordinary delta, apply only the missing same-domain constraint(s) in one filter call, assign the exact result, and save it under a fresh key. If the user explicitly replaces or corrects a category, search afresh using the replacement and all other active criteria rather than filtering an incompatible category-specific result. A cached entry that omits an active criterion is not complete.
rejected_edits.target: If a suitable cached base exists and a new constraint is not reflected in it, retrieve the latest suitable result using `get_results_from_cache(key="<exact key from the cache summary>")` and assign the returned result; do not rely on variables from earlier code or turns. Apply only the new same-domain filter and save the update under a fresh relevant key.
